title: Missing Number
contract: Input contains distinct values from 0 through n, with exactly one missing, where n is array length.
brute: for(int value=0;value<=a.length;value++){boolean found=false;for(int x:a)if(x==value)found=true;emit("Search for a candidate","value",value,"present",found);if(!found)return value;}return -1;
optimal: int missing=a.length;for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++){missing^=i^a[i];emit("Cancel each present value against the complete range","index",i,"xor",missing);}return missing;
reasoning: Search the input for every value in the complete domain until a missing one is found.
XOR the full range with all present values; equal values cancel.
Initialize with n because the loop covers indices 0 through n−1. The distinct bounded-domain contract is necessary; this is not a general missing-positive algorithm.
